I will do this year much like I did before, with a little push on fertilizer because 7.5 mu is not tiny, and if yield drops the loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on bags. Around here, if wheat looks weak in spring, people regret saving fertilizer, not using too much. I have well water, so I will not let the crop sit dry when it needs water. For wheat, I will keep a better seed that people nearby already planted and saw good ears from. I will give enough base fertilizer, then topdress with urea when it turns green in spring. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives grain if the stand is good. I will still follow the wheat-maize habit on the same 7.5 mu, rotary till the land after harvest, water on time, and spray when I see disease, worms, or too much grass. I do not like gambling with the harvest, so I will feed the land a bit heavy rather than light, but not so heavy that I waste money.
